resources.string: Pull a page down from the top to reload it.
Swipe sideways on the address bar to move between open tabs.
Tap twice on a page to zoom in on that spot.
When you copy a link elsewhere, offer to open it here.
Reopen the tabs you had when the browser starts.
Show suggestions while you type. Sends what you type to your search engine as you type it.
Request the desktop version of every site, not the mobile one.
A row of the sites you open most, on the home screen.
Show your bookmarks on the home screen.
Show the pages you visited recently on the home screen.
Most sites need JavaScript to work. Turning it off breaks many of them, and stops a lot of tracking.
Cookies let a site remember you between visits — that includes staying signed in.
Cookies set by other companies embedded in a page. This is how you are followed from site to site; blocking them rarely breaks anything.
Turning images off makes pages load faster and use far less data.
Let a site open a new window by itself. Usually advertising.
Choose a picture for the home screen.
Go back to the plain background.
Put the menu buttons back in their original order.
Return every setting to how it was on the first run. Your bookmarks, passwords and files are not touched.
Logins saved for sites, and a check for ones exposed in known leaks.
Cards for filling in checkout forms, stored encrypted on this device.
Your name, address and other details, for filling in forms in one tap.
Small pieces of code that change how a site behaves.
Reminders and meetings, with alarms and a calendar.
Documents you reuse — quotes, invoices, letters — that the assistant fills in for you.
Files the assistant has created: code, documents, archives.
Sequences you repeat, saved under a name so you can ask for them in a few words.
Browse the files on this phone.
Articles saved for reading without the page around them.
Whole pages saved to read without a connection.
Where downloaded files go, and what has been downloaded.
Add a provider and its API key. The assistant needs one of your own to answer.
